articleTitle: Impact of converters’ negative-sequence fault current injection on distance protection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The injection of negative-sequence current from Converter-based Resources (CBRs) during faults has been increasingly proposed and suggested in various international standards and grid codes such as the IEEE 2800 standard. As such injection changes the nature of the fault response of the CBRs, it can introduce uncertainties and risks to the existing AC protection. This paper presents comprehensive studies and analysis to evaluate the impact of Negative-Sequence Current Injection (NSCI) on distance protection. Realistic Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) tests are conducted using a commercially available distance relay, along with CBR models compliant with the grid code in Great Britain (without NSCI) and technical connection rule in Germany (with NSCI). The outcomes of this paper offer valuable insights to the system owners in different countries to understand the benefits, as well as potential issues, of the NSCI of CBRs from the protection perspective.

articleTitle: High-impedance grounding fault detection for resonant earthed networks considering capacitor switching
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Reliable detection of high-impedance grounding fault in the resonant distribution network is a challenging topic, which may be interfered by the capacitor switching action. The transient professes of high-impedance grounding fault and capacitor switching are theoretically analyzed, which explain the confused reasons of two signals from the traditional time-frequency characteristics. Then, the Lissajous curves are constructed by the zero-sequence waveforms of current and voltage, exhibiting significant distinction for different events in distribution network. By observing the changes of Lissajous curves, the characteristics of curve area and curve distortion are used to detect and distinguish high-impedance grounding fault and capacitor switching. An adaptive triggering criterion and a distortion complexity quantification index are designed respectively for the selected characteristics. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified through simulation experiments and field cases.

articleTitle: Transformer fault identification method using trajectory features of current sampling values
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: A transformer fault identification method based on current sample data is proposed in this paper. Mechanism and characteristics of transformer faults are analysed firstly. Transformer fault identification plane is proposed. It is divided into two parts: internal fault zone and external fault zone. The RTDS simulation results show that the method can identify transformer faults quickly and sensitively. It is not impacted by data window length.

articleTitle: Analysis on fault characteristics of MVDC distribution networks and applicability of protection schemes
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Medium-voltage DC (MVDC) distribution networks use flexible DC technology, but differ from MMC-HVDC transmission networks in topology, DC reactor configuration, etc., which leads to new fault characteristics of MVDC distribution networks. Existing DC protection techniques are unable to recognize these features in MVDC distribution networks, and identify the fault areas quickly and accurately. In this paper, the fault characteristics in MVDC distribution networks are theoretically analysed, concluded that the faults have the characteristics of rapidity, weak boundary and complex TW reflection characteristics. Fault characteristics of MMC converters and DC/DC transformers are also modelled and analysed, and confirmed through simulation. Existing protection technologies can hardly meet the requirements of both rapidity and selectivity. Some protection technologies act slow, unable to control the DC circuit breaker to cut off the faulted section before converter blocking, leading that bipolar short circuit can cause power cut in the entire MVDC distribution networks. Protection technologies such as single-ended TW protection based on boundary characteristics of DC reactors are difficult to achieve selectivity, because DC reactors are not configured at ends of the line to form a boundary between travelling waves or high-frequency transient signals.

articleTitle: A study on a current transformer modelling method considering core magnetic saturation characteristics for PSCAD/EMTDC
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes a current transformer (CT) model for PSCAD/EMTDC, which uses the Vrms-Irms excitation characteristic curve provided by the manufacturers along with the hysteresis loop-width as a percentage. The model effectively captures the nonlinear saturation characteristics and the core loss of a CT. Unlike existing models that require complex and often unavailable input data, this approach simplifies data input by directly utilizing the manufacturer's excitation curve. It performs piecewise linearization, ensuring that the voltage-current relationship follows the characteristics within each segmented region. To validate the accuracy of the proposed model, an open-circuit test was conducted using a voltage source-based equivalent circuit. The results confirmed that the proposed model successfully replicated the nonlinear behaviour of the CT under test conditions.

articleTitle: Reliability assessment of wind power DC collection systems considering energy storage devices
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The wind power DC collection system demonstrates significant development potential in overcoming issues such as harmonic resonance and reactive power transmission associated with traditional AC wind power collection systems. The reliability of the collection system is crucial for the safe and stable operation of the entire wind farm. This paper first analyzes the topological structure of the wind power DC collection system; then, it uses the Sequential Monte Carlo Method to assess the reliability of the wind power DC collection system; next, it optimizes the reliability assessment results using energy storage devices; finally, it analyzes the impact of energy storage devices on the reliability of the wind power DC collection system using a 100 MW wind farm as an example. The results indicate that energy storage devices significantly enhance the reliability of the wind power DC collection system.

articleTitle: Research on protection intertripping schemes for metro DC power systems based on goose network
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In conventional designs of metro DC power supply systems, signal transmission for intertripping functions, including bilateral intertrips of contact line protection, circuit breaker failure protection intertrips, and frame leakage protection intertrips, relies on control cables. This not only results in a multitude of circuits, high I/O demands, substantial cable usage, and intricate wiring topologies, but also lacks compatibility among protective relay devices from different manufacturers. This issue has become a key industry concern. Although some solutions have been put forth in previous research, they still have shortcomings. This paper comprehensively evaluates the pros and cons of the existing approaches and proposes a networked protection scheme based on GOOSE communication technology, which completely replaces control cables between protective relay devices, thereby ensuring reliable transmission of various intertripping signals. In the context of contact line protection, protective relay devices monitor the status of the bypass isolator to determine intertripped targets and directly issue trip commands, enabling efficient intertrips without the need for signal relay under the over-zone bilateral feeding operation condition. For breaker failure protection, two distinct intertripping schemes have been adopted and implemented on respectively on the protective relay devices associated with the incomer, regenerative braking, and feeder breakers. In frame leakage protection, four independent intertripping logics, designed to address current and voltage leaks in various DC cabinet frames, are implemented on negative pole protective relay devices, thereby ensuring precise control over the scope of intertrips. Finally, the real-time performance of signal transmission is theoretically analysed and validated, with comparisons made against other existing schemes. Through practical testing and analytical evaluation, the proposed scheme achieves networked DC protection for metros, characterised by a simplified and clear network structure, easy compatibility and expandability, comprehensive intertripping functions, and high real-time performance.

articleTitle: A novel non-pilot distance protection scheme for asymmetric short-circuit faults of transmission line with converters at both ends
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Both the renewable energy power station and the flexible DC converter are inverter-based power sources, where the output current's magnitude and phase are controlled, exhibiting weak feeding characteristics. In the line with converters at both ends, distance protection at both ends fails to operate correctly. This paper analysed the composite sequence network of asymmetric short-circuit faults in line with converters at both ends, and proposes a distance protection scheme immune to transition resistance, capable of accurately measuring the fault distance. By utilizing the changes in electrical quantities after the breaker trips at one end, a non-pilot protection scheme that does not rely on communication is introduced. This protection scheme uses different principles at both ends of line with converters at both ends. Simulation results show that the proposed protection can accurately identify asymmetric short-circuit faults in line with converters at both ends and can effectively and rapidly protect both the flexible DC converter and the renewable energy power station.

articleTitle: Transient short-circuit currents analysis of renewable energy sources considering multiple controller working stages
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The study of transient short-circuit current of renewable energy sources (RESs) can provide important evidence for the design principles and setting calculations of protection relays. However, existing transient short-circuit current calculation models for RESs fail to accurately characterize the response features of the controller under different working stages. For full-power inverter-interfaced RESs, this paper adopts the method of best square linear approximation to linearize the active powe r of photovoltaic, solves the fault component of the photovoltaic DC bus voltage. And then obtains a transient short-circuit current calculation model based on the power variation under the constant power control stage and the amplitude limitation control stage. For partial-power inverter-interfaced RESs, this paper simultaneously considers the rotor side converter control stage and the Crowbar control stage, proposes a transient short-circuit current calculation method based on the superposition of multiple responses, and achieves a unified expression of short-circuit currents at different control stages while ensuring local differences. Finally, a test system is built on the PSCAD/EMTDC, which demonstrates the feasibility and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: CNN-based sensitive earth fault detection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper explores the use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for sensitive directional earth fault detection in non-solidly grounded systems, aiming to enhance the reliability of fault detection. By training the CNN model with simulated datasets, the method has achieved accurate direction detection of permanent faults, transient faults, and transient intermittent faults. The test results show that this approach has yielded good outcomes in multiple tests, including those conducted by the KETOP lab, and the China Electric Power Research Institute (CEPRI) in Shaanxi and Liaoning. The paper provides detailed insights into the distribution of three-phase currents in faulted and unfaulted feeders, simulation parameters, composition of the detection algorithm, and deployment settings of the device.

articleTitle: Multi-ended line differential protection communication and time synchronization with HSR and PTP
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The increasing integration of distributed power sources, particularly inverter-based generations like wind and photovoltaic, has introduced significant challenges to traditional power grid protection schemes. This paper introduces a multi-ended line current differential protection scheme to enhance fault detection and isolation reliability within complex power grid topologies. Time synchronization, analogue values, and control signals are managed in parallel by the LineDiff data flow using different frame types over a common physical interface. The scheme utilizes High-Availability Seamless Redundancy (HSR) to ensure communication redundancy and employs the Precision Time Protocol (PTP) to achieve precise time synchronization among protection relays, with one relay designated as the master clock. The implementation of these protocols allows sub-microsecond synchronization without reliance on external clocks and reducing communication delays. The direct connection communication methodology using HSR and the establishment of a PTP time domain for multi-ended line current differential protection is also discussed in this paper. Following this, the resampling method aligns sampled values across different clocks enabling the utilization of data across various time domains. Finally, test results from time synchronization test, data synchronization test and operate time test are detailed, demonstrating that the LineDiff system meets all requirements.

articleTitle: The advancement of automated testing in protection relay systems:tackling key challenges and enhancing efficiency
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The field of automated testing in protection relay systems has advanced significantly, offering more efficient, accurate, and reliable testing procedures compared to traditional manual methods to deal with evolving challenges in protection testing. The future of automated testing aims to address these issues through improved closed-loop testing and advanced methodologies. Enhanced closed-loop testing introduces a feedback loop from the relay to the simulator, allowing dynamic modifications based on relay reactions for more accurate simulations. Modern automated testing solutions are scalable and flexible, accommodating various relay models and protection schemes. These systems reduce testing time, minimize manual intervention, and ensure high accuracy and consistency. As utilities adopt these advanced methodologies, the reliability and safety of electrical power systems will be significantly enhanced, ensuring a promising future for protection relay testing.

articleTitle: Low voltage ride-through for grid-forming renewable energy based on virtual impedance
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: During low voltage ride-through (LVRT) of grid-forming renewable energy sources, the typical control objective is to limit the current magnitude, often neglecting control over the injected power. This paper proposes a LVRT method based on virtual impedance, aiming to control power during the LVRT process of grid-forming inverters. The method ensures that the power during fault steady-state reaches the given reference while simultaneously limiting the magnitude of short-circuit current in steady-state conditions, thus enhancing grid support during fault ride-through. Finally, the proposed LVRT method is validated and confirmed through simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Pilot protection for flexible DC distribution line based on fault current difference
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Flexible DC distribution networks, known for their superior power quality, minimal line losses, and ease of control, are emerging as a key choice for future distribution network configurations. However, due to the limited fault current withstand capability of power electronic equipment, prompt action against faults must be taken within milliseconds. Purely protection-based fault handling often struggles to balance the stringent demands for speed and selectivity, and the existing protection is difficult to meet the requirements of speed and selectivity. Therefore, based on the analysis of the active current limiting characteristics of MMC converter and the fault current characteristics of DCSST, the requirement of protection quickness is relaxed reasonably, and the longitudinal protection method based on fault current difference is proposed. This method can achieve absolute selectivity, and does not require high-speed motion, low requirements on sampling rate and communication equipment, and has good resistance to transition resistance. The simulation results show the applicability of the proposed method in the flexible DC distribution network.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of the energization of a distribution feeder with temporary protective grounding connected
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the voltage and current levels to which workers are exposed during maintenance of a distribution network in the event of accidental re-energization. Simulations of the energization of a real distribution feeder, with temporary protective grounding connected were performed using ATPDraw software. Assuming that the temporary protective grounding was appropriately installed, several simulations were performed changing the system characteristics, such as feeder lengths, ground rod resistance and soil resistivity. Additionally, single-phase energization and the bracket grounding method were simulated. The voltage and current levels that the worker and the temporary protective grounding cables would be exposed were verified, as well as the voltages between the point where the temporary protective grounding was connected and the ground. The results demonstrate that in some accidental energization the current and voltage levels exceed the established safety limits for the workers. The IEEE 1048 standard, which provides guidelines for the application of temporary protective grounding in transmission and distribution lines, warns against the use of bracket grounding systems where single-phase energization could occur. However, the simulations indicate that voltages and currents exceeding safety limits can also occur during a three-phase energization.

articleTitle: Single-ended protection of AC transmission line based on fault traveling wave energy ratio
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: When the renewable energy is sent to the sending end of the system through the flexible direct transmission system, the fault characteristics will be affected by the control strategy of the power electronic converter on both sides of the line. In view of the above problems, the research of fast protection scheme is very important for large-scale renewable energy exchange system. This paper first analyzes the transmission path of traveling wave when the line fails and the frequency distribution of traveling wave when the fault occurs inside and outside the area. Due to the difference in the frequency distribution of the traveling wave when the fault occurs inside and outside the area, the wavelet packet transform is used to characterize the energy of each frequency band. The ratio of high and low frequency energy of the fault traveling wave is proposed as the criterion for fault identification inside and outside the area. Finally, the protection method is established and verified by PSCAD / EMTDC. The simulation results show that the proposed protection scheme can correctly identify internal and external faults. The method is simple and has strong resistance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: A novel adaptive harmonic phase measurement method suppressing harmonic and noise interference
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The harmonic measurement algorithm based on the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) faces challenges with poor anti-interference capabilities and significant degradation in measurement accuracy under noise interference. To address this issue, we propose a harmonic phasor measurement method that considers both harmonic and noise interference. First, a band-pass filter bank is used to filter out noise in the broadband measurement signals, reducing its impact on measurement accuracy. Next, the Interpolated Discrete Fourier Transform (IpDFT) algorithm accurately retrieves the parameter information of the fundamental and harmonic phasors. Finally, the initial measurement value of the IpDFT is corrected through the amplitude compensation to achieve accurate measurement of the fundamental and harmonic phasors. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide a frequency error below 5mHz and an amplitude error below 10-2% for all harmonic phasors from the first to the fiftieth order under scenarios of harmonic distortion and noise interference generated according to the IEC60255-118-1 standard.

articleTitle: Fault direction discrimination and protection technology for distribution net-works under high proportion distributed photovoltaic connection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The flexible integration of high proportion distributed photovoltaics into the distribution network has led to significant changes in the fault characteristics of the distribution network, especially the four quadrant load characteristics of distributed photovoltaics, which directly leads to the failure of current fault direction discrimination technology. Hence, the design of an effective protection system for distribution network with multiple inverters is a complicated engineering challenge. This paper introduces a novel protection method using a current-only polarity comparison. The proposed method is based on the phase difference between the pre-fault and fault current components. The method provides a new way to identify faulted sections and possible construction of pilot protection suitable for distribution networks. Simulations are conducted using PSCAD/EMTDC software.

articleTitle: Steady-state fault current calculation method of LFTS with offshore wind farm integration considering converters’ control strategy
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Low frequency transmission system (LFTS) has become a competitive method for long-distance offshore wind power transmission. The fault current of LFTS is strongly coupled with the control strategy of converters. This paper proposes a novel steady fault current calculation method considering strategies including modular multilevel matrix converter (M3C) and grid-side converter (GSC) of an offshore wind farm. Firstly, the fault equivalent circuit model based on external characteristics of converters is derived, which is used for phase current calculation at both ends of the submarine cable. Then, the expressions of arm currents in M3C are derived. The distribution of high-frequency component and low-frequency component among nine bridge arms is influenced by the control strategy of M3C. Finally, simulation results show the correctness and high accuracy of the proposed calculation method. The fault current calculation method can be applied to equipment selection and relay protection of LFTS with offshore wind farm integration.

articleTitle: Non-unit protection for HVDC grids based on wavelet analysis of transient voltage
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: DC grids utilizing MMC-HVDC technology have been extensively researched and implemented in various locations, demonstrating substantial benefits in terms of system flexibility and renewable energy integration. Due to the rapid escalation of fault currents, DC line protections must quickly identify and isolate faults, typically within milliseconds, leading to the adoption of non-unit methods as the primary protection. This paper introduces a non-unit protection scheme that employs transient voltage at both the line-side and converter-side of the supplemental inductor. Based on a reduced model focusing on the boundary of a DC line, the transient process of the fault is examined using traveling wave theory, and the voltage characteristics at both ends of the supplemental inductor are scrutinized. The theoretical analysis also brings out a practical method for threshold-value calculation. Then, a protection criterion, based on wavelet analysis of the transient voltage, is established. This proposed method is capable of fulfilling the requirements for speed, selectivity and fault resistance and has been verified through PSCAD/EMTDC simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the influence of secondary double fault of neutral point non-effective grounding distribution line on protection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The construction of a secure and reliable distribution network is a critical component of smart grid development. Overhead distribution lines, constantly exposed to atmospheric conditions, are susceptible to faults caused by lightning, strong winds, snow, and other external weather events. In recent years, the increasing frequency of extreme weather has resulted in more complex characteristics, such as the tics of the distribution-line faults. Under adverse weather conditions, transient single-phase grounding in distribution lines can lead to double-phase faults in adjacent lines and simultaneous lightning strikes on multiple lines can cause short-circuit faults. Current fault detection and relay protection technologies for distribution lines primarily address simple faults, and their ability to handle secondary double faults or multiple fault events requires a thorough investigation. This paper focuses on secondary double faults in overhead distribution lines within non-effectively grounded distribution networks. A simulation model of the overhead distribution network was established to investigate the occurrence of double-phase short-circuit faults triggered by single-phase grounding along adjacent lines. Characteristic measurements of complex faults were obtained and theoretically analyzed for accuracy. Based on these findings, the adaptability of existing overcurrent protection for distribution lines was analyzed.

articleTitle: The impact of voltage-dependent current injection on power swing characteristics in grid-following VSC systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of voltage-dependent current injection (VDCI) during fault ride-through (FRT) on power swing characteristics in grid-following voltage source converter (GFL-VSC) systems. The analysis reveals that power swing dynamics in GFL-VSCs are primarily influenced by the phase-locked loop (PLL) output angle,δPLL, and the current phase angle,φ. The findings demonstrate that VDCI during FRT helps to dampenδPLL oscillations and reshape impedance trajectories, with a larger k-factor further restricting their range. Theoretical results are validated through PSCAD/EMTDC simulations.

articleTitle: Applicability of current protection in distribution system containing Thyristor controlled hybrid Transformer
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The Thyristor Controlled Hybrid Transformer (TCHT) is a novel flexible interconnection device used to achieve interconnected power supply and power flow regulation in distribution networks. However, it introduces changes in the fault characteristics of distribution network lines, which may lead to unreliable operation of relay protection devices, thus affecting system stability. To ensure the safe and stable operation of the distribution network, this paper proposes a method for analyzing line faults in distribution networks containing TCHT and thoroughly examines the impact of faults on current protection. Initially, this study investigates the principles and control characteristics of TCHT, with particular emphasis on the impact of Low Voltage Ride Through control strategies during line faults in the distribution network. Subsequently, it analyzes the fault characteristic s of distribution network lines containing TCHT during interphase short circuit faults, exploring the specific impact of these faults on the various components of three-stage current protection. Finally, the analysis is validated through simulations on the PSCAD/EMTDC platform, highlighting significant changes in the fault characteristics of distribution network lines containing TCHT. This study provides a theoretical basis for the design of protection systems in distribution networks with TCHT.

articleTitle: Equivalent simulation model for integrated control and protection of commonly used converters in low voltage DC power distribution
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The analysis of low-voltage DC systems requires the use of a variety of converters and complex coupling relationships. Consequently, system simulation is the most effective method for the analysis of the operating characteristics of such system s. However, the traditional converter modelling method is complicated, and it is difficult for distribution designers to complete the modelling of multiple converters in a short time. In order to improve the simulation efficiency of power distribution designe rs and standardise the modelling process and results, this paper proposes a commonly used converter equivalent model topology capable of realising the simulation and analysis of system control and protection characteristics by taking the four main features of steady state function, dynamic performance, external fault characteristics and protection function as the indexes, and analyses and gives a scheme on how to configure the corresponding control and protection functions. Finally, an equivalent model of converter control and protection is established for the commonly used converters in the system. Comparison of the simulation results with the experimental results shows that the proposed equivalent model can meet the requirements of the converter model in the simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Optimal solution to design and implement centralized protection system in 11 kV Al Ain Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to provide an optimal solution to isolate the faulty zone when the bus faults occur in 11 kV Distribution Network using centralized Protection system without any additional investment. Due to rapidly growing power demand in Al Ain Distribution network, the numbers of 11 kV Distribution Network feeders are more and protection system cost also have been increased. Normally, the protection scheme available in Al Ain 11/0.415 kV Distribution network is designed to be isolate the fault when fault occur in the Distribution transformer feeders. Moreover, there are no protection in Distribution substation Incomers and/or outgoing feeders except Earth fault Indicator. Therefore, the problem is, during incomer/outgoing feeder cable/OHL fault, the fault would be cleared by remote end 33/11 kV primary substation feeders. In many cases, 33/11 kV Primary substation power transformers were tripped, when the outgoing feeder fail to clear the fault, which would cause AADC networks KPIs. Also, operator should identify and isolate the faulty line based on fault locator indicator. Hence, providing power supply to customer is within short period of time is paramount. The successful protection can be achieved subject to compliance of speed, selectivity, sensitivity, reliability, and stability. Speed always refers to isolate the fault with less or no damage to the system. Selectivity always refers to isolate only the faulty zone without interrupting the healthy zone. Sensitivity means to sense the condition only in the fault situation to isolate the fault while stability refers to keep the system stable in order to keep the healthy zone uninterrupted when the outside zone is in fault condition. It is possible to make sophisticated protection schemes using IEC 61850 with GOOSE communication. However, the solution would not be cost effective as communication devices such Optical Fiber Cable (OFC), Switches, etc. and relevant accessories and maintenance cost will tremendously increase. Hence, overcome the issue is that the solution to design protection scheme using centralized protection system without compromising, safety, security, reliability and speed as minimal cost is always possible. As latest IEDs having more protection settings groups and more no. of current/voltage input to measure fault current for overcurrent and earth fault relays. While Settings Group-1 (SG-1) is used as graded overcurrent/Earth fault protection for feeder -1, Settings Group-2 (SG-2) is used for feeder -2, and so on. The logic is formed in the Centralized protection System to activate relevant setting group based on fault condition and related faulty feeders will trip and isolate the fault by relevant setting group, if the fault current is above the set value as the fault current measured by the relevant feeder current transformer, thereby a major outage could be avoided, and outage will be limited to the faulty zone. More care should be taken while adopting the protection settings and scheme in order to isolate only the faulty and remining feeders should be remain without any power supply interruption. Also, operation team patrolling time/cost would be eliminated as present situation is identify the faulty feeders as the Incomer/Outing feeders are with cable fault locator only. Therefore, this concept is prepared in consideration to provide an economical, safe, secure, and reliable scheme with utmost care in order to minimize the damage to equipment and ensure continuity of power supply to customers as far as practicable. This solution is to implement in the Brick Built distribution Substation (BBSS) network as well as 11 kV Switching Stations (SWS), where more number of feeder available.

articleTitle: Directional protection for power networks connected with inverter based renewable resources
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The global installed capacity for renewables is expected to increase by ~85% by 2050. This shift is being driven by climate goals, energy security, and economic factors. Unlike fossil fuel-based generation, renewables are integrated into the power grid through power electronic converters. The main challenge posed to directional protection is the unique fault response dictated by converter controls and grid codes. Decades-old directional protection algorithms including polarization designed based on conventional understanding are inadequate and reported several practical relay failures from various power utilities. To mitigate these challenges, a positive sequence current based directional method is proposed. In this method, a reference signal is computed using the average of positive and negative derivative of the positive sequence fault current. The directional index is obtained as the difference between the angle of the reference signal and the angle of the positive sequence fault current component. The direction of fault is identified as FORWARD if the directional index is in the range [−45°, 45] and REVERSE if the directional index is in the range [−225°, −135°]. The proposed method is verified for various test systems and test scenarios and the performance of the proposed method is superior as compared to conventional methods. The proposed method is validated with field data and its performance is satisfactory. The proposed method is independent of line and source impedance settings and is not impacted by converter controls and grid codes.

articleTitle: Fault location for collection lines in DC series-parallel offshore wind systems using multiscale Sobel gradient algorithm
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: DC series-parallel systems are a critical technology to the development of distant offshore wind power. Unlike in conventional DC networks, collection lines in DC series-parallel systems are short and have uneven segmented structures in which DC transformer (DCT) capacitors are connected in series with submarine cables, which exerts tough challenges to existing fault location methods. To overcome the limitations, this paper proposes a single-ended traveling wave fault location method using the multiscale Sobel gradient (MSG) algorithm. Firstly, this paper elaborates on the configuration of a DC series-parallel system and discusses the specificity issues. Then, the impact of series DCT capacitors on the boundary characteristics and the wave propagation paths in collection lines are analysed. On this basis, the MSG algorithm is utilised to identify the traveling wavefronts with distinct polarity and the fault location is determined accordingly. Finally, the proposed location method is evaluated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform. The results verify that the method can acquire accurate fault distance regardless of fault type and fault resistance, and is robust against noise interference.

articleTitle: Control strategy improvement and differential protection improvement of flexible low frequency transmission system
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Due to the power electronic converter on both sides of the low frequency transmission line, the fault current is limited in amplitude and uncertain in phase under the influence of the converter control, which is difficult to adapt to the conventional relay protection. In this paper, two control strategies, negative sequence current suppression and negative sequence current injection, are used to analyze the adaptability of current differential protection on the low frequency side of modular multilevel matrix converter. Because of the difference of fault characteristics under different control strategies, it may lead to the rejection of conventional differential protection. The traditional current differential protection has the problem of low sensitivity. In order to improve the sensitivity of differential protection, the traditional differential protection is improved first, and then the co ntrol strategy is improved. Two control strategies of negative sequence current injection and negative sequence current absorption are proposed, and a high sensitivity current differential protection principle suitable for low frequency transmission system s is proposed. Finally, the corresponding electromagnetic transient simulation model is constructed in PSCAD/EMTDC, and the verification results show that the M3C low frequency negative sequence current injection proposed in this paper is suitable for different fault types.

articleTitle: Time-frequency mutation characteristics-based pilot protection for offshore wind power DC transmission lines
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: DC collection and transmission systems offer high efficiency, compact size, and eliminate the need for reactive power compensation, positioning them as the future trend for offshore wind farms. However, submarine transmission cables possess significant distribution capacitance compared to onshore overhead lines. During an external fault, the distribution capacitance current in long submarine cables causes obvious current differences between both sides of the line, potentially leading to th e mis-operations of traditional pilot protection systems based on transient measurements. To address this issue, this paper proposes a pilot protection principle based on the time-frequency mutation characteristics of fault currents. By analyzing the transient current frequency characteristics of the DC transmission line and converter, the frequency band differences between the two sides of the transient fault current are considered for both internal and external faults, and the appropriate frequency band for protection application is selected. The time-frequency transformation of fault currents is performed using wavelet transform, and the identification criteria for internal and external faults are constructed using the Wasserstein distance. This approach addresses erroneous operations in pilot protection systems based on transient time-domain quantities for external metallic or low-resistance faults. The offshore wind power DC collection and transmission system model is constructed in a Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS), and the proposed protection scheme is simulated and verified. Hardware-in-the-loop simulation results show that the proposed protection method reliably identifies all fault types, with protection action times of less than 5 ms, transition resistance up to 300 Ω, and noise immunity up to 20 dB.

articleTitle: A single-end protection method of DC lines for MMC-HVDC grids using graph Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Module multilevel converter-based HVDC (MMC-HVDC) grids request direct current circuit breaker isolate fault lines within 6ms after faults, which requests protection method output trip signal within 3ms. The main technical difficulty is quick and reliable fault identification for DC lines of MMC-HVDC. This paper proposes a single-end protection method using graph Fourier transform (GFT) of 1-mode voltage fault components to realize fault identification. First, the paper presents the frequency characteristic analysis of the 1-mode voltage fault component between internal and external faults. Then, the graph Fourier transform is introduced into the relay protection for DC lines. Use the weighted path graph to encode the sampling sequence of 1-mode voltage fault components in the sliding window to a graph signal. Perform the GFT on the graph signal and use the highest-order graph Fourier transform spectrum coefficient as the input of the protection method. Finally, a fault direction criterion using GFT and a single-end protection method using GFT are proposed, respectively. The proposed method is verified on the four-terminal DC grids built in PSCAD/EMTDC. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. The method outputs the detection results within 1 ms and is sensitive to internal high-resistance faults.

articleTitle: A pilot differential protection of HVDC transmission lines considering the influence of DC voltage divider
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In this paper, considering the influence of the transient characteristics of DC voltage divider and the line distributed capacitance current on protection, a pilot differential protection of HVDC transmission lines considering the influence of DC voltage divider is proposed. Based on the circuit model of DC voltage divider, the transfer function of DC voltage divider is derived, and the transient characteristics of DC voltage divider are analyzed. Based on the theory of equal transfer process of transmission lines (ETPTL), the current signal is processed by virtual digital DC voltage divider to solve the problem of inconsistent transmission characteristics between voltage and current. When the line voltage is processed by a low-pass filter with a sufficiently low cut-off frequency, it can be considered that the line voltage is linearly distributed along the transmission line. According to the fitted characteristics of voltage distribution along the transmission line, the distributed capacitance current of the line can be calculated by integral calculation. Simulation results show that the proposed method can quickly and reliably identify faults in different fault scenarios, and has high resistance tolerance.

articleTitle: Fault current calculation method for flexible HVDC grid considering the DC unified power flow controller
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes a generic short-circuit fault current calculation method for Flexible HVDC grids. The calculation procedure begins from modelling the fault circuit of the MMC converter station as an RLC circuit, and then constructs the fault network matrix of flexible DC grid during the fault occupation. Meanwhile, considering the dynamic characteristic of DC Unified Power Flow Controller (DC-UPFC), analytical formulas for fault current under different current limiting stages of DC-UPFC is obtained. The proposed approaches are validated by comparing with the electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation results on PSCAD/EMTDC. Cases study showed that the calculation method can be easily used to evaluate the severity of a dc fault under different current limiting stages, which lays the foundation for subsequent research on the impact of DC-UPFC fault current limiting parameters and the coordination of DC circuit breaker (DCCB) operation timing.

articleTitle: A novel instantaneous energy spectrum based traveling wave fault location method for MTDC offshore grids
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: An accurate and reliable DC fault location method is crucial for enhancing the resilience of offshore MTDC grids. The performance of existing double-ended Traveling Waves (TWs) fault location methods is significantly affected by factors such as sampling frequency and noise disturbance. To address these issues, this work proposes a novel TWs-based fault location method using the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and the Hilbert transform. First, the TWs propagation under DC fault conditions is presented. Then, high-frequency intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) containing fault location information are extracted using the VMD algorithm; The fifth mode, IMF5, is transformed by the Hilbert transform to obtain its Instantaneous Energy Spectrum (IES). Based on this, the arrival times of the TWs can be precisely calculated. Finally, the fault location is estimated by combining the TWs velocity on both sides of the line with the arrival times. A typical 525 kV three-terminal MTDC model is built on RTDS simulation platforms. The results show that the proposed fault location method provides accurate fault location results and can withstand 35 dB of noise interference in a real-time testing environment.

articleTitle: Identification of key parameters for suppression of continuous phase change failure in UHV DC transmission based on digital twin model prediction
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: As the core device of the conventional DC transmission project (LCC-HVDC), the thyristor converter valve itself does not have the shutdown capability, which easily induces the occurrence of phase change failure. Continuous phase-change failure mainly occurs in the phase-change recovery process after the removal of the AC short-circuit fault at the receiving end, which is mainly due to the improper DC control recovery strategy. The existence of the dynamic switching power topology behaviour of the commutator valve and the nonlinear coordination mechanism of multi-objective control in the LCC-HVDC transmission system makes it show strong time-varying and nonlinearities during the fault of the AC line at the receiving end, and it is impossible to establish the accurate DC control strategy and the continuous phase-change failure through a simple calculation. control strategy with the accurate mathematical relationship between continuous phase change failure. To address this problem, this thesis proposes a key parameter identification method for suppressing continuous phase change failure of UHV DC transmission based on the prediction of digital twin model. Firstly, the short-circuit current output characteristics of LCC-HVDC under the fault of the receiving AC system are grasped and an equivalent model of the AC-DC hybrid grid based on the receiving AC bus of the converter station on the inverter side looking to the sending end is further established, and then based on the equivalent model, real-time Then based on this equivalent model, a real-time closed-loop fast simulation + error recapitulation method is used to clarify the key parameters of continuous phase change failure suppression, and the effectiveness of this paper's method is verified based on the CIGRE Benchmark model simulation.

articleTitle: A resilience enhancement method for power systems against malicious cyberattacks
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: With the rapid development of information and communication technologies (ICTs), it is crucial to study how power systems can improve their resilience against cyberattacks. A resilience assessment and enhancement method for power systems is proposed for malicious cyberattacks on substation intelligent electronic devices (IEDs). A hidden semi-Markov chain model is developed to analyse the attack process and the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (VCSS) framework is applied to investigate the compromise of IEDs. An optimal power flow-based model is used to evaluate the consequence and risk of the power grid under malicious attacks on the IEDs. A defender-attacker-defender model based on limited defence resource allocation is developed to enhance the resilience of the grid against the attacks. The proposed method is tested on the modified IEEE reliability test system (RTS-79).

articleTitle: Simplified modeling method for full-power converters under positive and negative sequence separation control
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Current gird codes require that renewable plants absorb negative-sequence inductive reactive current to suppress the rise of negative-sequence voltage. However, it increases the complexity of simulation model since full-power converter is required to have the ability to control both positive and negative sequence components, which brings great challenges for the simulation efficiency of large-scale converter-based system. To address the problem, this paper proposed a novel simplified modeling method for full-power converters considering relay protection requirement. Due to the isolation of the DC link, the fault characteristics mainly depend on the control strategy of grid-side converter. Hence the simplified model focuses on the representation of the grid-side converter. Neglecting the complex switching process of power electronic devices, this paper retains converter’s function and represent it with mathematical differential equations based on the conservation of power and control strategies. The simulation results shows that the simplified method can improve the simulation speed while ensuring the simulation accuracy. The proposed method can be used for modeling the power system with large-scale renewable energy sources to achieve fast simulation, which provides the support for relay protection analysis.

articleTitle: Advanced protection strategy for real time mitigation of field loss in synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Traditional methods for detecting Loss of Excitation (LOE) in synchronous generators (SGs), specifically impedance-based methods, face challenges in terms of delayed response time and mal-operation during power system disturbances (PSDs) or non-LOE (NLOE) events. In this regard, a novel strategy for fast and accurate identification of various events using the negative sequence voltage component (VLN) of terminal voltage and rotor angle deviation (▵δ) of the SG is presented. The LOE and PSDs conditions are discriminated by utilizing sudden variation in rate of change of power(▵P⁄▵t).An advanced LOE detection index (ADLOEI) is introduced to monitor such events. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by generating various scenarios on the developed phase-domain model of the generator in real-time digital simulator (RTDS). The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can detect LOE events more reliably and quickly than the conventional scheme and offer better security during PSDs (stable power swing (SPS) and out-of-step (OOS) conditions).

articleTitle: Holistic cyber security solution on substation automation system
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The way grids are operated and managed has changed dramatically due to the integration of renewable and decentralized energy resources, the need for network optimization, the interaction with prosumers and consumers, and the participation of new market entrants. With information and communication technology penetrating down to the distribution network, the growing interconnections create more points for potential attacks to critical infrastructure. This paper describes a holistic cybersecurity solution on substation automation system, based on security principles "Defense in depth principle", "Least privilege principle" and "Network Segmentation". A holistic cybersecurity solution protects the whole system from 3 parts: People, Process, Products and system, make sure every ‘member’ in the system is secure and not vulnerable to exploitation.

articleTitle: A new distance protection method using calculated voltage as polarization voltage for renewable energy system
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Vigorously developing renewable energy represented by wind power and photovoltaics has become an inevitable choice for the world. The continuous and rapid growth of renewable energy generation represented by wind power and photovoltaics has made the scenario of renewable energy stations being connected to the AC power grid through super AC transmission lines a typical scenario in the power system. However, studies have shown that for renewable energy systems, the adaptability of distance protection is insufficient due to the influence of converter control strategies. Therefore, this paper aims to construct an improved distance protection suitable for renewable energy AC transmission lines to solve this problem. This article takes the AC transmission lines of renewable energy stations integrated into the AC power grid system as the research object, and proposes an improved phase to phase distance protection principle that combines directional criteria and fault location criteria. The directional criteria are used to identify forward faults, including faults within the area and faults outside the area. Based on this, the fault location criteria further identify faults within the area, and the two work together to achieve protective exit actions.

articleTitle: Design of time synchronization system for intelligent electronic devices in new type power systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: As a distributed and decentralized system across geographic space, the new type power system needs to maintain the accuracy and reliability of time synchronization in different regions. Time becomes the data foundation attribute for monitoring and control the new type power systems. An Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) time synchronization system based on IEEE C37.238 is proposed, which adopts a coordinated mode of CPU and FPGA modules. Besides implementing the IED specific functions, CPU module completes the following time synchronization functions: Precision Time Protocol (PTP) message encoding and decoding, using the peer-to-peer delay measurement mechanism to calculate the clock offset and clock syntonization, time information interaction with FPGA, and initialization of FPGA and PTP protocol stack. FPGA module achieves the functions below: detecting PTP event messages, generating event message timestamps by the hardware, maintaining local clock, and providing a variety of local clock adjustment mechanisms such as coarse adjustment and fine adjustment. Hardware and software coordination ensures microsecond-level synchronization accuracy. CPU selection is very flexible according to the function and performance demands of different IED, which makes it easy to expand and upgrade. FPGA is functionally independent and can remain unchanged, which reduce the whole device cost.

articleTitle: Control method and protection design for multi-station parallel operation of island microgrid system
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Independent micro-network systems powered by distributed power generation (DG) such as wind, light, storage and diesel generators are increasingly used in remote areas and island scenarios. With the growth of the number of microgrids (MG), the interconnection of multiple micro-grid systems with close distance to improve the power supply economy and reliability through connecting lines has gradually become a topic worthy of attention and exploration. Based on two micro-network systems on an island in Hong Kong, this paper designs a control method for the dual-station parallel operation of the master station-substation mode: the master station maintains the system frequency and voltage reference value, and the substation and the master statio n cooperate to achieve power balance and voltage stability; At the same time, the operation strategy will maintain the balance of the battery state of charge (SOC) of each station, and maximize the ability of power supply support between stations. The protection design of the system mainly includes the following aspects: photovoltaic generation (PV) and wind generation Power Conversion System (PCS) failure and system disconnection; In case of failure of energy storage, switch the load power supply path through the circuit breaker, and switch the role positioning of master station and sub station if necessary; Cut off the faulty line and adjust the operation mode of each micro-network station in case of failure of connecting line; Treatment of too low or too high stored energy SOC. The dual-station parallel system mentioned above has been in stable operation on site for one year and has achieved the design expected results. The control method and protection design can be extended to more micro-network system interconnection scenarios.

articleTitle: A model identification pilot protection scheme that accounts for the active current limiting of MMC
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The half-bridge MMC (Modular Multilevel Converter) possesses active current limiting control capabilities, which can reduce the system’s requirements for the breaking capacity of the DC circuit breaker, conducive to the economic and stable operation of the flexible DC power grid. However, most existing protection principles are influenced by changes in fault characteristic s after the active current limiting control is activated, making it difficult to reliably identify the fault area. In response to this issue, this paper establishes a line impedance model for internal and external faults using the time-domain current difference and voltage difference between the two ends of the line, and introduces a similarity algorithm to reliably identify the fault area. By integrating the start-up criteria and fault polarity criteria, a model identification pilot protection scheme that accounts for the active current limiting of MMC is proposed. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme is not affected by the engagement of current limiting control and maintains high sensitivity and reliability under a 800Ω transition resistance and 30dB noise interference.

articleTitle: Ice fault identification and adaptive reclosing strategy for transmission lines based on multi-source information fusion
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In order to meet the requirements of adaptive reclosing for fault cause and fault characteristic identification, this paper proposes a fault identification and adaptive reclosing strategy of transmission lines in winter based on weather information. First, the statistical characteristics of fault and reclosing operation of transmission lines in winter are analysed. Second, the occurrence of transmission line faults in winter under specific weather conditions is counted, revealing the correlation between the fault causes and weather information. Then, using DS evidence fusion theory, a Bayesian statistical model of weather conditions and a waveform image recognition model are fused to identify the cause of transmission line faults. Based on the identified fault causes, combined with the prior knowledge of the success rate of fault reclosing and the time of ice-shedding bounce, an adaptive reclosing strategy is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by inversion of several fault cases.

articleTitle: Research on overcurrent mechanism and suppression strategy for MMC-HVDC DC fault recovery
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In MMC-HVDC systems, DC-side faults lead to severe over-currents in the bridge arms, causing the blocking of the insulation gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) and the shutdown of the MMC-HVDC system. To enhance fault recovery performance, this paper analyses the over-current mechanisms caused by IGBT unblocking and proposes a novel fault recovery control strategy. First, it highlights the inevitability of the underdamped MMC-HVDC fault loop leading IGBT blocking. Second, it is revealed that the root cause of IGBT unblocking over-current is the voltage disparity between the DC and AC sides. Then, the proposed method involves removing the power outer loop of the MMC during IGBT blocking and adjusting the AC side modulation waveform to mitigate the voltage difference. Additionally, considering the sub-module capacitor voltage and reclosing timing during blocking, an adaptive power outer loop reference value curve is constructed to eliminate the overvoltage problem due to surplus power. Test results indicate that, compared to the existing method, the proposed method can reduce the peak bridge arm current from 1.68 p.u. to 0.79 p.u. under the worst conditions, significantly improving system resilience.

articleTitle: Research on fault crossing characteristics and islanding protection mechanism of medium voltage distribution lines under phase to phase short circuit
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The flexible integration of large-scale distributed energy resources and the enhanced interaction between users and the power grid have increased the operational complexity and state uncertainty of new distribution networks featuring high-penetration distributed photovoltaics. This poses greater challenges to the already strained protection technologies of distribution networks. The fault ride-through performance of distributed energy resources in distribution networks and their anti-islanding protection characteristics are not well-defined, and there is a lack of coordination between the protection control strategies of various safety and stability automatic devices, which are considered the third line of defense in the power system. This results in significant safety operation risks and fails to effectively support the stable and secure operation of regional power grids. This paper studies the fault ride-through characteristics of distributed photovoltaics under inter-phase short circuits in medium-voltage distribution lines, as well as the differences in electrical characteristics of distributed photovoltaics during system disturbances and unplanned islanding operations. It analyzes the operational behavior of anti-islanding protection in the fault handling process and proposes a new anti-islanding protection principle for distribution networks that is coordinated with the third line of defense, along with its tuning and coordination methods. The effectiveness of the proposed solutions is verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Adaptive protection scheme in modern distribution networks based on proximal policy optimization
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The worldwide trend of energy transition has thoroughly reshaped the structure of modern power distribution systems. With the proliferation of grid-edge elements such as distributed generation, energy storage and electric vehicle, the sensitivity and reliability of conventional distribution protection methods is greatly undermined. In this paper, we use the state-of-the-art machine learning algorithm to design a novel protection mechanism that can accurately detect and respond to faults under circumstances where conventional protection can be difficult to configure and function. The proposed approach is implemented and tested in a variety of fault simulations and is shown to achieve superior performance especially under complex operating conditions.

articleTitle: A two-terminal traveling wave fault location method for distribution network using directional traveling waves
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The distribution network is an important link connecting the transmission network and electric power customer, and its power supply reliability directly affects the user experience. Two-terminal traveling wave fault location of distribution network has high accuracy, and is less affected by factors such as line operation mode, fault resistance, transformer conversion error, uneven line parameters along the corridor. After a fault occurs, it can quickly locate the fault and reduce the line patrol time. Usually, fault location systems have their own centralized master station. It is difficult to integrate the centralized master station of the fault location system into the distribution automation master station. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a new method for two-terminal traveling wave fault location in distribution networks using directional traveling waves for on-site intelligent distributed lightweight master stations. This method does not require the construction of a centralized master station, which reduces investment. FTU (Feeder Terminal Unit) is also an on-site fault location master station, reducing computation and data traffic. The proposed method has guiding significance for traveling wave fault location in distribution networks.

articleTitle: Performance of distance protection under inverter-based resources with IEEE 2800 current injection requirements
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Under fault ride-through (FRT) mode, inverter-based resources (IBRs) are required to meet current injection requirements in emerging grid codes. The impact of IBRs on system protection may vary depending on the requirements, further challenging the operation of protection system under the influence of IBRs. In this paper, we focus on the impacts of IEEE 2800 current injection requirements on distance protection. First, we develop a specified current-limiting scheme to comply with the IEEE 2800 standard. During unbalanced faults, the impacts of the current injection on apparent impedance are elaborated analytically. In a modified IEEE PSRC D29 system with IBRs, the performance of distance protection is investigated under varying impact factors, including K factors, fault proximity, and fault resistance. The results indicate that the specified scheme alters the magnitude and angle of current vectors, thereby modifying the trajectory of apparent impedance. With the specified current-limiting scheme, the sensitivity of distance protection is improved since the current capacity is fully utilized, but the rapidity of protection decreases due to the phase current scaling when the K factor is large. Hence, the selection of K factors should be based on the converter current capacity of IBRs.

articleTitle: Long-term planning model for electricity-hydrogen coupled storage system in distribution networks with high proportion of renewable energy integration
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: To deal with the impact of the ultra-high proportion of distributed energy resources (DERs) integration on active distribution networks (ADN), a novel planning model with electricity-hydrogen coupled energy storage technology is proposed in this article. Considering the unpredictability of the widespread of DERs, it is necessary to take long-term scale into consideration to further regulate the real-time output of the coupled storage system. In a case study of IEEE-33 system, the comprehensive planning result is obtained, the operating cost of ADN is minimized and the detailed comparison is analysed result shows that coupled storage system have economic advantages compared with single battery storage system in nominal scenarios. Further analysis in extreme scenarios fully demonstrates the good adaptability of the coupled system to cope with adverse DERs output. Meanwhile the coupled storage system maintains better economic performance. The model provides reference for the future planning of ADN.

articleTitle: Required footing resistance for critical oil & gas overhead distribution lines
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The majority of the electrical loads that are essential for the extraction, transfer and processing of the Oil and Gas products are scattered along vast areas and fed through thousands of kilometers of 13.8kV and 34.5kV overhead lines. Those networks traditionally demonstrate elevated failure rates against transient faults caused by lighting activity, mainly due to their low critical flashover voltage levels and the high specific resistivity of the ground. Obtaining and sustaining low-enough grounding resistance values is a decisive factor in the flashover rates of the self-restoring insulation and the effectiveness of the installed surge arresters to protect the non-self-restoring insulation.

articleTitle: An improved line sampling value current differential protection method considering capacitive current
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: A sampling value analysis plane was constructed to visually analyze the drawbacks of existing sampling value differential protection, and a new principle of fast longitudinal current differential protection using sampling value current was proposed to address these issues. The proposed improvement criterion has been adjusted and optimized for the protection braking zone on the sampling value plane. The optimized braking range is only related to the size of the capacitor current and is almost unaffected by the converter control strategy. While ensuring the reliability of faults outside the zone, it greatly improves the sensitivity of faults within the zone, and still has good adaptability in the scenario of new energy transmission.

articleTitle: Adaptive restart scheme for HVDC transmission system based on voltage injection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Rapid restarting of high-voltage DC transmission system after a fault is crucial for the stable and reliable operation of the system. Conventional restart methods have the disadvantages of blindness, long restart process, and high restart failure rate. Restarting on permanent fault will cause more impact on the system or lead to system shutdown. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an adaptive restart scheme based on voltage injection. First, a fault property identification mode based on open-loop voltage control and closed-loop current control is proposed to be incorporated into the LCC control system. Secondly, the change rule of line voltage and current in the fault identification stage is analyzed based on the equivalent circuit diagram of the system under temporary and permanent faults. Finally, an adaptive restart scheme for HVDC transmission system based on voltage injection is proposed. The proposed scheme realizes the injection of voltage signals into the system after fault isolation while limiting the system current, which improves the safety of the system during fault restart. The proposed scheme can be realized based on the existing control system without additional equipment. The scheme has good noise and interference immunity, and its realization has a low sampling rate requirement, which has a good prospect for engineering applications. An electromagnetic transient model of the LCC-HVDC transmission system is constructed in PSCAD/EMTDC based on the engineering parameters, and simulations are carried out for verification. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can correctly recognize the property of faults and can realize the restart of the system after the fault.

articleTitle: Real-time wavelet-based undervoltage protection for active distribution networks
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The continued integration of distributed renewable resources has facilitated the emergence of active distribution networks. However, distributed generators will feed fault currents from the load side during faults, imposing higher demands on fault detection and isolation in active distribution networks. Undervoltage protection plays a crucial role in fault isolation on the load side, and improvements in this area can significantly enhance the protection performance of active distribution networks. This paper proposes a real-time wavelet-based undervoltage protection for active distribution networks. It decomposes the time-domain three-phase voltages into wavelet and scale coefficients, offering an affordable computational burden. The high-frequency and low-frequency fault information embedded within the wavelet domain is utilized to develop an improved undervolt-age protection criterion. Verified through PSCAD/EMTDC software simulations, the proposed protection demonstrates enhanced sensitivity in fault detection and rapidity in fault isolation across various fault conditions. The proposed approach lever-ages modern digital signal processing algorithms to enhance traditional techniques, aligning with the conservative nature and developmental trends in the protection field.

articleTitle: Research on first commutation security domain of LCC-HVDC transmission systems considering AC faults
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: At present, line-commutated converter high voltage DC (LCC-HVDC) is the main force of long-distance cross-regional large-scale transmission. With the emergence of multi-infeed DC (MIDC) transmission system, the single fault of the receiving-end AC system may lead to the first commutation failure of several LCC-HVDCs at the same time, causing a large amount of power shortage in the receiving-end power grid, which seriously affects the safe and stable operation of the power grid. In this paper, the influence of the inverter firing angle and the commutation voltage of the AC side on the first commutation process is analyzed. The first commutation security domain considering different AC fault types and parameters is established. Based on the analysis of the security domain, it is considered that the fault detection time and the control response time are the key to the mitigation of first commutation failure. The correctness of the proposed security domain and the influence of the detection/response time on the mitigation methods are verified by simulation. The research results lay a theoretical foundation for the first commutation transient security domain and the first commutation failure suppression method.

articleTitle: Voltage support ability assessment of grid-forming converters integration in power systems
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: As the installed capacity of renewable energy continues to increase, the inertia and short-circuit capacity of the system continues to decline, arising significant risks for the power system security.
