The grid-forming technologies is of great significance in solving this problem, attracting wide attentions. Compared with the grid-following converters, the grid-forming converters have good frequency and voltage support capabilities, and have great application prospects in the context oflarge-scale grid-connection of new energy sources. The aim of this paper is to investigate the voltage support ability of the grid-forming converters on power systems. Firstly, a voltage support capability indicator is proposed for the voltage stability issues. Secondly, a mathematical model of the grid-forming converter is developed to investigate its active and reactive power support characteristics. The key parameters of the grid-connected renewable energy are identified via the proposed indicator. On this basis, evaluation indexes for grid-connected renewable energy to improve the voltage support capability of the system are proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed evaluation methodology is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent identification method for CT abnormal in busbar protection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Bus protection generally adopts differential principle protection, which uses branch current to synthesize differential current and braking current, and trips the outlet to cut off the bus fault. Therefore, busbar protection heavily relies on current transformers, which must be wired correctly, and the transformation ratio and polarity must meet the characteristics requirements of relay protection. Otherwise, differential protection misoperation can cause large-scale power outages and even threaten the stability of the power grid. The current transformers for busbar protection can be divided into busbars, sections, lines, transformers, and other branches. Based on the characteristics of busbar protection, this article proposes an intelligent identification and analysis method for busbar polarity, transformer polarity, and line polarity. The polarity reversal of current transformers is one of the causes of bus protection accidents. Intelligent identification of the polarity of current transformers in bus protection can eliminate potential accidents in advance, which is of great significance for the stable operation of power systems. Bus protection is the most important protective equipment in substation. Once there is misoperation or refusal to operate, it can cause damage to power equipment and huge loss of power supply. Busbar protection generally adopts the principle of Percentage biased differential current, which combines differential current and restraining current from the currents of each branch of the busbar. After fault diagnosis, it trips and cuts off the busbar fault. Therefore, busbar protection heavily relies on the performance of current transformers (CTs), and the phase sequence, transformation ratio and polarity of CTs must be correctly connected to the equipment, otherwise it will cause differential protection to malfunction and reject. The connection branches of busbar protection can be divided into busbar, section, line, transformer, etc. There are differences in the differential current performance of various branch currents. Based on these characteristics, this article proposes an intelligent identification and analysis method for busbar polarity, transformer polarity, line polarity, and disconnection. This article is based on Kirchhoff's law and sampling point algorithm, using the balance correlation between large and small differential currents to identify the polarity and disconnection of the busbar CT, using the phase and amplitude similarity of differential current and branch current in the transient process of transformer excitation inrush current to identify the CT polarity abnormal branch, and using the phase and amplitude similarity of differential current and capacitor current in the charging process of the line to identify the CT polarity abnormal line. This article proposes a solution to distinguish between faults and disconnection based on sensitive voltage and zero sequence current, in order to address the problem of false blocking in high resistance faults using disconnection algorithm of current transformers in busbar protection. And for each part of the intelligent recognition principle, this article analyzes and verifies it through simulation or citing on-site fault data. Reverse polarity and wire breakage of CT are one of the causes of bus protection accidents. Intelligent identification of CT polarity and wire breakage in bus protection can eliminate accident hazards in advance, which is of great significance for the stable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: An accurate and fast short-circuit faults isolation scheme for distribution system with distributed generator integration
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: As the world commits to reduce carbon emissions, more and more Distributed Generators (DGs) and power electronic devices are integrated in distribution systems. In existing protection methods for distribution lines considering the integration of DGs, achieving precise fault isolation is challenging for overcurrent element due to the difficulty in time coordination and the selection of setting values. Traditional differential element requires high data transmission capability and data synchronization accuracy. This paper proposes a new scheme for precise and rapid isolation of short-circuit faults in distribution lines with DGs integration. Based on fault characteristic differences between forward and backward faults, the scheme determines fault direction locally and share fault direction information between adjacent terminals. A new differential protection criterion and short-circuit fault isolation scheme are further constructed. The new scheme combines the advantages of localized protection and communication-assisted protection, significantly reducing data transmission volume. Additionally, the new scheme does not interrupt electricity supply for transient faults, and provides precise and rapid two-ended isolation for permanent faults. This creates the foundation for restoring power to non-faulted sections, thereby improving the reliability of electricity supply in distribution systems at a low cost.

articleTitle: Current differential protection data synchronization scheme for active distribution networks based on nodal voltage phasor
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Two-terminal and multi-terminal current differential protection (CDP) is an effective means to solve the protection problem of active distribution networks (ADN), but the problem of data synchronization limits its application. The fault moment self-synchronization method provides practical means for differential protection in the distribution network. On this basis, this paper first proposes a fault moment self-synchronization method based on nodal voltage phasor. In this scheme, the relative synchronization errors between each terminal are obtained by comparing the voltage phasors calculated by each terminal to realize data synchronization. Combined with the dual starting logic, the proposed scheme can solve the data synchronization problem of two-terminal and multi-terminal differential protection in special scenarios such as weak feed and unloaded mode without additional investment, and provide a new idea for the engineering application and popularization of multi-terminal differential protection. Simulation based on PSCAD-MATLAB verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method under different fault conditions.

articleTitle: Improvement methods for low-frequency load shedding strategies in substations with distributed energy storage
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In cases of grid emergency control failure and system frequency decline beyond limits, substation low-frequency load shedding devices maintain system stability by sequentially shedding bus loads. However, current low-frequency load shedding strategies disconnect all loads and energy storage through feeder breakers, failing to utilize distributed energy storage to support critical loads. Firstly, this paper improves the existing substation low-frequency load shedding model by constructing a dual-layer decentralized control substation low-frequency load shedding model. This model achieves independent control of regular loads and distributed energy storage on feeders, ensuring that energy storage can remain operational during low-frequency load shedding without being affected by feeder load shedding. Secondly, a new method for calculating load shedding amounts in rounds based on energy storage is established, correcting the round iteration strategy. Additionally, an optimization method for invoking feeder distributed energy storage in the ancillary services market is proposed to reduce costs and incentivize energy storage participation in supply security. Finally, a simulation comparison analysis is conducted using a 10kV feeder of a substation and the IEEE 33-bus system, verifying the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed model and methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of key factors affecting travelling wave fault location in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Fast and effective fault localization helps to restore the faulty line in time, while for distribution network fault ranging, there is still no reliable means of fast and accurate fault localization. The main problems are: the complex structure of the dist ribution network, the variety of load types, the traveling wave propagation process is complex; the length of the distribution line is relatively short, the fault ranging algorithms have higher accuracy requirements; the zero-mode wave speed varies greatly with the frequency of the traveling wave, and the wave head frequency is higher, which also puts forward higher requirements for the measurement device. This paper firstly analyzes the traveling wave propagation characteristics in distribution networks, analyzes the factors affecting the initial traveling wave head, and discusses the applicability of the existing ranging methods; secondly, it analyzes the characteristics of the zero-mode wave speed change in distribution networks, and discusses the impact of the traveling wave speed determination method on the accuracy of traveling wave ranging in distribution networks; finally, for the current commonly used wavelet transform algorithms cannot accurately find the traveling wave head, and analyzes the problem of the initial traveling wave head. Finally, we analyze the effect of the initial traveling wave head on the traveling wave ranging accuracy in view of the problem that the current commonly used wavelet transform algorithm cannot find the traveling wave head precisely. Combining theoretical derivation and simulation analysis, this paper analyzes the key factors affecting the traveling wave ranging accuracy of distribution networks, and provides a reference for improving the traveling wave ranging accuracy of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Study on the fault protection mechanism and optimal configuration of SFCL for photovoltaic-energy storage-direct current-flexibility system
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The Photovoltaic-Energy storage-Direct-Flexible system (PEDF) is an innovative distribution system in buildings. This study theoretically derives the transient fault characteristics of the PEDF system and analyzes the fault current limiting mechanism of superconducting fault current limiters (SFCLs) in this context. It is proposed to install a hybrid SFCL at the converter outlet of the battery, where the fault impact is most severe. A comprehensive assessment of the current-limiting effects and economic viability of the SFCL led to the identification of the optimal configuration scheme. Finally, a simulation model o f the PEDF distribution system was established using PSCAD/EMTDC software, integrating the SFCL optimization model at the designated location. Simulation results validate the proposed scheme's feasibility, providing a basis for the fault protection strateg y of the PEDF system.

articleTitle: A non-isolated DC/DC converter with active fault protection module for all-DC offshore wind DC turbines
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The all-DC collection and transmission for offshore wind power is an ideal scheme for offshore wind power collection and transmission. Medium voltage DC/DC converters for wind turbines are one of the key technologies for all-DC collection and transmission. A non-isolated DC/DC converter (NIC) with active fault protection module suitable for offshore DC wind turbines is proposed. The capacitor in the traditional boost circuit is reconnected to form a new structure, and two structures are ca scaded together to increase the voltage level. To solve the problem of high current stress in the front end, a module is stacked in the front end. The modular design reduces the design difficulty. The end uses an active back-end that can adjust the output voltage and can block DC short-circuit faults. The active back-end circuit can still operate normally when some sub-modules fail, thus improving the system’s reliability. The DC short-circuit fault-blocking capability. The designed converter has an input parallel output series structure. The proposed converter requires fewer series-parallel modules and fewer components, has fault-blocking capability, has low current stress, low cost, small size, and high efficiency. The simulation results verify the validity of the proposed DC/DC converter.

articleTitle: A calculation method of electrical quantities during faults for distribution network with grid-forming inverter-based resources
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Traditional fault analysis and calculation methods based on synchronous generator are not suitable for distribution network integrated with distributed generators (DGs). Existing research focuses on the grid-following (GFL) inverters, while grid-forming (GFM) inverter-connected distribution network are less studied. This paper proposes a fault calculation method for the scenarios of GFM Inverter-Based Resources (IBR) integration. First, the control strategy of virtual synchronous generator (VSG), which is one type of the GFM inverter, is studied. The characteristics of active power output are analyzed for VSG during distribution network faults. Based on a typical distribution network, a fault equivalent model for VSG-type DG integration is developed. Then, a fault calculation method is proposed using the relationship between power and voltage/frequency. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method offers high calculation accuracy.

articleTitle: Comparative study of current-, voltage-, and distance-based fault identification and protection coordination for DC distribution and microgrid
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In this paper, different types of DC distribution protection methods, including overcurrent, current derivative, undervoltage, and distance protection, are studied. Their performance at different operating conditions (e.g. loading current, system transients, configuration changes, inrush) and fault conditions (e.g. fault resistance) are evaluated. The issues at challenging conditions are described and analysed. Different protection methods are compared in terms of protection speed and performance. Each method has its own pros and cons. In actual systems, different methods may be applied together to overcome specific problems.

articleTitle: 22-kV protection system improvement HK Electric
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: 22-kV closed-ring network has been adopted in HK Electric for more than 20 years. As compared with its 11-kV open-ring counterpart, it has proven its improved performance in terms of supply reliability and power quality. While each cable section in the 22-kV network is protected by pilot wire protection, no unit protection is provided for switchgear fault in order to simplify our protection design and maintenance work. This design philosophy is proved to be effective but there were still a few occasions of switchgear fault in which the fault had to be isolated manually by System Control. This has led to longer than usual supply restoration time. To further enhance our supply reliability and power quality under different fault scenarios, HK Electric has reviewed its protection systems and has come up with a new protection design philosophy. This paper describes the original design of 22-kV protection system for the closed-ring network in HK Electric, its pros and cons and the difficulties encountered since its introduction in early 2000s. It is followed by the review of the 22-kV closed-ring network. At the end of the paper, a revised 22-kV protection scheme is proposed to further enhance our supply reliability and power quality without over-complicating the distribution protection design.

articleTitle: The correction method for faulty travelling wave distortion of transmission lines integrated to offshore wind farm
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: As known, the accuracy of traditional traveling wave fault location algorithms is highly dependent on the calculation of the initial traveling wave velocity, which is highly correlated with the precise acquisition of the traveling wave spectrum. Especially, for the transmission system integrated to offshore wind farms, it generally adopts undersea cable transmission line, which includes complex transmission medium and highly coupling with sea water or ground. When a fault occurs on the line, the high-frequency transient traveling wave generated by the fault point propagates along the line to both ends, and afterwards amplitude attenuation and frequency distortion phenomenon occur during the propagation process due to electromagnetic coupling issue. Therefore, the correction algorithm needs to be studied which should have the ability to obtain the original traveling wave information based on the highly distorted traveling wave information. Based on this, the following work has been done in this article: (a) the frequency dependent characteristics of undersea cable transmission line and converter station boundaries are studied, and the frequency distortion phenomena is analysed; (b) the frequency spectrum correction algorithm, which has the ability to recover original traveling wave spectrum from highly distorted traveling wave spectrum, is illustrated; (c) the ±400kV HVDC transmission system integrated to offshore wind farm is established via PSCAD/EMTDC, and the accuracy and robustness are proved.

articleTitle: Analytical calculation of DC fault current of 12-pulse actively commutated current source converter
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Current-source-converter (CSC) is a promising topology for constructing a novel DC transmission system with the breakthrough of new generation reverse blocking integrated-gate-commutated-thyristor (RB-IGCT) device. Under HVDC transmission scenarios, the 12-pulse CSC topology is usually adopted to enhance the harmonic characteristics and system capacity. Fault characteristics can provide a basis for system planning as well as protection design. However, the exsisting researches can hardly describe the DC fault characteristics of 12-pulse CSC quantitatively. Therefore, an analytical calculation method of DC fault current of 12-Pulse CSC is proposed in this paper. The point-of-common-coupling (PCC) decoupled fault equivalent model is introduced in this paper to realize order reduction for 12-pulse CSC, based on which, the fault current calculation method is derived. The proposed method can calculate the DC fault current of 12-pulse CSC analytically and more accurately compared with the conventional method, which can facilitate the fault characteristic analysis. The proposed calculation method is validated through PSCAD/EMTDC simulation.

articleTitle: A modern retrofit solution for induction disc overcurrent relays
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Entering the 21st century, the migration of power grids from a reliable but inflexible system to a “Smart Grid” is an inevitable trend. This presents a challenge for utilities as they need to enhance their existing legacy equipment. Moreover, utility grids have an installed base of protection relays from various generations, which poses a challenge when a particular generation, such as electromechanical and static protection relays, reaches the end of its service life. To address these challenges, the utility identified the necessary requirements and collaborated with a relay manufacturer to develop a feasible retrofit solution for its significant installed base of Electromechanical Induction Disc Overcurrent & Earth Fault protection devices (EM OCEF). This paper discusses a retrofit solution whereby the existing EM OCEF relays can be withdrawn (racked out) from their cases, while leaving the panel AC and DC wiring intact. Subsequently, a numerical protection relay can be directly plugged in to replace the EM OCEF relay. This solution requires minimal to no wiring modification work, offering a practical and efficient approach to modernizing the power grid infrastructure. This paper further describes the manufacturer’s design and utility’s approval testing of the retrofit kit, which includes laboratory testing and an extensive field trial. The laboratory testing included functional and simulation tests of the protection and EMC tests and environmental tests. To assess the circuit outage period required, the utility organized a demonstration installation at its electrical workshop, where the retrofit kit was successfully installed in a transformer panel. The demonstration showed that the entire installation process met the target requirement of less than 4 hours, completing the task in approximately 1.5 hours. Following the successful laboratory testing and demonstration installation, the utility organized a field trial for the retrofit kit. The retrofit kit was successfully installed at two customer substations within the utility’s distribution network, replacing an EM OCEF relay with a numerical protection relay. The on-site retrofit kit installation was completed in under 2 hours, with 1 hour dedicated to the existing wiring checks, modification and relay replacement and another hour for pre-commissioning and commissioning tests. The field trial demonstrated the effectiveness of the retrofit concept, which was approved by the utility in September 2023. In contrast, a traditional retrofit solution would typically require a full day for a site visit, including the measuring of the panel cut-out for a new relay replacement, planning for wiring modifications and identifying safety precautions for the panel cutting. Site work alone would take at least 6 hours or longer to install the new relays, seal the cut-outs, rewire the system and conduct commissioning tests. The retrofit kit solution precisely meets the utility's needs by allowing the replacement of an old secondary device in a streamlined manner within a limited outage time, while also reducing the risk of incorrect wiring. Additionally, the retrofit solution delivers digital protection, offering several additional benefits such as disturbance and event recording, measurements and self-checking in accordance with the latest substation standards.

articleTitle: The ideal solution to high-speed busbar transfer in complex power supply scenarios
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: HSBT (High Speed Busbar Transfer) device, especially the device with new HSBT design, plays a vital role in ensuring safety in industrial continuous production as well as in power transmission processes through uninterrupted power supply. These devices can transfer to the backup power source within 200 milliseconds after the loss of primary power source, greatly improving the reliability and stability of the power system. They are not only widely used in the petrochemical industries and power plants but are also popular in other fields where power supply continuity is critical. However, most HSBT devices on the market have design limitations and are mainly aimed at relatively simple and typical application scenarios, such as single busbar with double power sources, sectionalized busbar with double power sources, and single busbar with three power sources. With the continuous improvement of customers' requirements for the reliability of the power system, there are more complex application scenarios, such as sectionalized busbar with 3 power sources, double busbar, etc. For such complex application scenarios, combination usage of multiple traditional HSBT devices is often required, which not only increases the complexity of configuration, but also increases the difficulty of maintenance, resulting in higher costs. In contrast, the device with the new HSBT design demonstrates its superior adaptability and flexibility. 1 device can handle complex application scenarios independently instead of the combination of multiple devices, significantly reducing maintenance and saving costs. The customers can freely select and configure input and output modules according to their specific application scenarios, and easily customize a high-speed transfer device with different transfer directions and transfer priority groups that fully meets their requirements. In summary, the device with new HSBT design is the ideal solution to ensuring power continuity and system safety in complex power scenarios due to its powerful performance, flexible configuration, and ease of maintenance. By simplifying the process of equipment configuration and maintenance, it not only improves the overall efficiency of the power system, but also brings significant cost benefits to customers. In the context of increasing complex power networks, the device with new HSBT design undoubtedly represents the development trend of future power management technology, providing a solid guarantee for power continuity in the industrial and commercial fields.

articleTitle: Current protection relay for distribution networks based on positive-sequence superimposed component trajectory
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The occurrence of uncertain power flow makes the setting of overcurrent protection more complex, since the power flow is no longer simply from-bus-to-load with the integration of renewable energy. Therefore, it is crucial to propose a novel protection relay that is immune to this scenario. Towards this end, this paper proposes a novel protection relay for distribution networks based on the superimposed-component phasor trajectory. First, the distribution characteristics of the positive-sequence superimposed component (PSSC) is analyzed, upstream or downstream. Then, the affinity clustering algorithm (ACA) is used to identify the faulted line in combination with line classification. Finally, a searching algorithm is proposed, and the last stage faulted line is considered as the origin of the PSSC, which will determine the faulted sub-feeder. PSCAD/EMTDC-based simulation studies show that the proposed protection relay can accurately find the faulted feeder with very high sensitivity and reliability.

articleTitle: Protection coordination of directional overcurrent relays in distribution networks with dispersed embedded generation
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Embedded generation (EG) connected to the radial power distribution network (RPDN) introduces several challenges for utilities, particularly in terms of protection. This necessitates the use of directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) in conjunction with conventional overcurrent relays (OCRs) to ensure proper coordination. However, coordinating these relays becomes challenging due to the location of EGs, which, if not properly managed, can lead to nuisance tripping. This research paper emphasizes the need for DOCRs and their new protection settings, particularly when EGs are sparsely dispersed in the network. The protection coordination issue is addressed by proposing a new methodology for determining the tripping decision of DOCR through threshold parameters and zero sequence ( If-zero seq ) symmetrical component. The performance of the proposed methodology is validated through 108 nodes CSIRO network in DIgSILENT PowerFactory. The improved parameter settings for DOCRs and OCRs provide enhanced time coordination, enabling fast isolation of the affected area. The proposed approach is applied considering three network segments. The simulation results demonstrate the capability to isolate faulted segments, thus forming an islanded scenario for continued supply, thereby effectively reducing the loss of energy to the customers.

articleTitle: Analysis and improvement of secondary operation circuits in smart substations
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: To reduce the problems of the secondary operation circuits in smart substations, this paper starts with a detailed analysis of two issues: the mismatch between two sets of intelligent terminal contacts leading to abnormal integrated accident signal of the intelligent terminal, and the mismatch between the reclosing charging logic of the protective device and the energy storage time of the closing spring resulting in multiple reclosing of the circuit breaker. Based on this, targeted improvement measures are proposed, and a special situation is analyzed. It has shown that the implementation of these improved measures has significantly reduced the occurrence of corresponding types of defects, indicating the strong practical value of this paper.

articleTitle: Faulted line identification in power distribution systems using convolutional neural networks and natural frequencies of travelling waves
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Accurate and efficient identification of faulted lines in power distribution systems is essential for maintaining a reliable and continuous electricity supply, particularly as these networks increase in complexity due to the integration of distributed energy resources (DERs). Traditional fault detection methods are increasingly challenged by these evolving conditions, necessitating the exploration of more advanced solutions. This paper proposes a novel approach that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs), trained on natural frequencies of fault-originated travelling waves to identify faulted lines. By applying the modified Baum-Liu-Tesche (BLT) equation, the natural frequencies are accurately calculated, serving as indicative features associated with different lines in the power network, specifically focusing on the first section of the IEEE 34-bus feeder. The proposed CNN model effectively learns to distinguish among seven classes of natural frequency distribution patterns, achieving peak classification accuracies of 94.99% and 92.63% in single phase-to-ground (1p-g) and three phase-to-ground (3p-g) fault scenarios, respectively. The robustness of the model is also validated across a range of fault scenarios, including different fault types, impedance, and locations.

articleTitle: Impact of grid forming inverter settings on distance protection overreach
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In inverter-based resource (IBR)-dominated power systems, protection challenges have grown increasingly complex, especially for distance relays designed for traditional synchronous generator behavior. This paper explores the impact of grid-Forming (GFM) inverter settings on distance protection relay overreach, focusing on Zone I overreach triggered by Zone II faults. Then, a unified sequence network model is developed to analyze how GFM control parameters, such as active power reference and virtual impedance, influence relay-measured impedance during short-circuit (SC) faults. It is revealed that, under line-to-line (LL) fault, increasing the active power reference significantly reduces calculated impedance in line-to-ground (LG) and LL faults, heightening the risk of relay overreach. In contrast, changes to the virtual impedance cause only minor impedance fluctuations with limited impact on overreach. The theoretical analysis is validated through electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations.

articleTitle: Initiatives on enhancing protection reliability in a distribution network
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Pilot Wire Differential Protection has been a well-established and cost-effective protection scheme in the distribution network of CLP Power Hong Kong Limited (CLP Power), which enables fast fault clearance within a protection zone. However, unfavorable condition of pilot wire may affect the security and reliability of its operation. Unwanted operation has escalated due to undetected pilot condition. In addition, repairing of pilot wire requires lengthy investigation and significant engineering effort. Even though unfavorable pilot conditions had been identified in past cases, unwanted operations still occurred in advance of pilot fault repair, contributing to extra customer minute loss. To further improve the protection reliability of the distribution network, CLP Power has recently implemented initiatives to enhance Pilot Wire Differential Protection scheme, including the Pilot Wire Supervision Scheme, the External “Plug & Play” Time Delay Device and the advanced Digital Current Differential Scheme. This paper outlines how CLP Power applies Pilot Wire Differential Protection Scheme, reviews the challenges posed by pilot wire with any abnormal conditions, discusses the technical considerations and installation arrangement of the initiatives.

articleTitle: Resonance and delayed zero-crossing effects in offshore facilities with variable shunt reactors
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The operation of interconnected offshore facilities with high penetration of variable shunt reactors (VSR) is presented as a study case. This paper unveils operating scenarios with VSR that lead to both resonant frequency and delayed zero-crossing phenomena not only at the switched breaker/cable, but also at distant interconnected platforms. To illustrate these findings a study case is presented based on an Arabian Gulf project consisting of over 220km of 230kV submarine cable and seven (7) distributed VSR for a total compensation of 750Mvar. The system studies were developed in PSCAD in which simulation results for delayed zero-crossing and resonant frequency are discussed as well as their impact in interrupting devices and relaying scheme. The paper concludes by proposing a set of operational constraints, protection scheme and shares waveform captures from a commissioned 230kV 120Mvar VSR point of wave switching controller to minimize these phenomena effects in EHV interconnected offshore facilities.

articleTitle: Investigation of conventional distance protection with single-pole tripping for six-phase feeder protection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The conversion of an existing double-circuit three-phase (3Φ) transmission line into a single six-phase (6Φ) feeder presents a practical solution for enhancing power transfer capacity, because as shown in [1-6] it can operate at a higher phase-to-ground voltage. However, as compared to double-circuit 3Φ lines, possible fault conditions in a 6Φ feeder are notably more complex, with 23 significant fault types and 120 fault combinations. In addition, single-pole tripping is now essential, as disconnecting an entire 6Φ EHV feeder for a fault that involves only one-phase, or even a few phases, is unacceptable from a system stability standpoint. In our previous research [6], a phase-segregated current differential protection scheme that only tripped the faulted phases was shown to operate correctly for all fault types. This paper evaluates the applicability of conventional distance protection using DIgSILENT PowerFactory® with two standard 3Φ “Micromho” relays [7] and special tripping logic.

articleTitle: Impact analysis of grid-forming control on sequence-component-based protection under asymmetrical faults
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Grid forming (GFM) control significantly alters the fault characteristics of the power systems, posing challenges to conventional sequence-component-based protections, including directional and phase selection elements. This paper develops a unified sequence network model for GFM inverter-based resource (IBR)-dominated power systems, identifying the specific control loops that impact sequence-component-based protection. It is revealed that the current-limiting control loop significantly influences the X/R ratio of IBR equivalent sequence impedances, further adversely affecting protections relying on negative-sequence components. The theoretical analysis is validated through controller hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) tests.

articleTitle: Machine learning-based anomaly detection method for digital substation against false data injection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The digitization in the grid space has broadened its attack surface resulting in an increased risk of cyber threats targeting critical power systems. Consequently, existing Protection, Automation, and Control (PAC) systems must be equipped not only to detect network abnormalities (e.g., fault) but also to identify anomalous cyber-attack patterns. This paper proposes a novel deep learning-based approach for detecting anomalous traffic in digital substations. The proposed approach uses Back Propagation Neural Network (BP) with Whales Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to detect False Data Injection Attacks. Backpropagation Neural Networks (BP) helps to identify complex attack patterns in smart grids while the Whales Optimization Algorithm (WOA) addresses the issues of slow convergence and overfitting and improves the overall performance. The proposed method is tested for a typical distribution substation with 2 power source feeders and 4 load feeders, modelled using the Digsilent PowerFactory simulation tool, yielding promising results with a 99% recall rate and 91% accuracy rate.

articleTitle: Modelling of cable insulation local defect degradation faults in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Cable lines are the primary type of urban distribution network, and their reliable operation is crucial for the safety of urb an power distribution. Cable faults mainly include line breaks caused by external force damage and developmental faults resulting from localized insulation defects. While fault detection and protection technologies have made significant progress in addressing externally induced faults, such as line breaks, leading to high rates of fault detection or isolation, they face challenges in quickly handling developmental faults arising from localized insulation defect deterioration. These types of faults exhibit intermitt ent and high-resistance characteristics in their early stages and undergo a prolonged development process, potentially resulting in permanent ground faults or even cable trench fires. Current research has focused on early fault warning based on temperature and local discharge characteristics but primarily applies to cable joints rather than cable insulation layers. Furthermore, there are gaps in the analysis of mechanisms and modelling. This paper analyses the mechanism behind the degradation process of localized insulation defects within cable insulation layers. It categorizes this process into three fault stages: transient non-penetrating flashover, semi-stable penetrating flashover, and stable penetrating flashover. The study establishes a comprehensive model that characterizes the randomness and intermittency associated with each stage of development. Through simulation and empirical data validation, it confirms the accuracy of this model. The proposed model provides a theoretical basis for studyi ng early fault warning systems for cables while also aiding in fault identification efforts. This work holds positive significance for reducing power grid accident risks and mitigating potential line hazards.

articleTitle: Transverse negative current fault location and protection for dual-circuit outgoing lines of inverter-based source
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: To enhance power system reliability and ensure the safety of substations, the utilization of dual-circuit outgoing lines in engineering projects is common for inverter-based power sources like photovoltaic power stations and direct-drive wind turbines. The fault characteristics of these dual-circuit lines differ significantly from those of single-line configurations. In the case of single-line, the fault current on the substation side is typically limited and contain minimal negative-sequence component due to the control mechanisms of the station's inverter. Conversely, in dual-circuit line, a fault occurrence in one line allows for the flow of considerable short-circuit currents and negative-sequence currents through the parallel non-faulty line in reverse direction. In order to tackle this issue, this paper proposes a novel principle for fault location based on transverse negative-sequence currents, specifically designed for dual-circuit outgoing lines of inverter-based power sources. This principle takes advantage of the negative-sequence current suppression inherent in inverters and achieves fault distance measurement by evaluating the relative ratio of negative-sequence currents in both lines. Building upon this theoretical foundation, a corresponding transverse fault protection scheme based on negative-sequence currents is presented. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of this scheme, demonstrating its capability to accurately identify both internal and external asymmetrical faults while remaining immune to fault transition resistances.

articleTitle: A novel distance protection for outgoing line of grid-forming inverter based on transient fault characteristics
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The grid-forming inverter is crucial to the high-penetration renewable energy power systems. When a fault occurs on the outgoing line of a grid-forming inverter, especially when voltage at the point of connection (POC) drops below the minimum voltage specified for low-voltage ride-through, a significant transient overcurrent will be generated, posing a risk to the safety of the inverter equipment. Therefore, it is essential to have fast-acting protection to isolate the fault promptly. This paper first analyses the changes in the control system of a grid-forming inverter with a dual-loop voltage-current control structure immediately after a fault occurs, and its impact on the switching states of the inverter's IGBT. Subsequently, an equivalent model of the inverter connected to the outgoing line is established. Using this model, the frequency domain transient fault characteristics of voltage at the inverter end of the outgoing line are analysed for both three-phase ground faults and two-phase short circuits. Based on these characteristics, a novel distance protection scheme for the outgoing line of the grid-forming inverter is designed for the aforementioned fault types. The proposed protection scheme is characterized by fast response time. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified through PSCAD/EMTPC simulations.

articleTitle: Sensitive turn-to-turn fault protection for power transformers using incremental negative-sequence differential and advanced stabilising criteria
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The paper presents a novel sensitive turn-to-turn fault protection scheme for power transformers based on incremental negative-sequence differential current. Detecting turn-to-turn faults (TTFs) in power transformers is very challenging since the fault currents measurable at the terminals are low. On the other hand, the power transformer protection must not operate in regular operating and switching conditions, such as transformer energisation or external faults. Present protection schemes based on negative-sequence differential current are briefly presented and discussed, as the proposed method represents a further development of these methods. It is based on the determination of the incremental negative-sequence differential current or the delta deviation between the pre-fault and fault state. For reliable discrimination of TFFs from adverse conditions, the restraint quantity in an operating percentage characteristic and two novel powerful stabilisation criteria were devised. This paper demonstrates the superior performance in terms of security and safety of the proposed protection scheme by discussing selected transients of TTFs and external faults obtained with a Real-Time Domain Simulation (RTDS) model of an autotransformer in a high-voltage network.

articleTitle: Feasibility of achieving fast RoCoF-based LOM protection – a case study of Hong Kong distribution network
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) are playing a critical role in the energy landscape to facilitate the decarbonisation of energy systems. One of the key requirements for the safe integration of DERs is to ensure the Loss of Mains (LoM) protection is sufficiently dependable and secure so that it can effectively detect islanding conditions while avoiding maloperation during other non-LOM grid disturbances (e.g. faults). This paper aims to assess the feasibility of achieving fast and reliable islanding detection using a commercially available Rate of Change of Frequency (RoCoF) based LoM relay. The study is undertaken on a section of the distribution system in Hong Kong (HK) where fast LoM protection operation (<260ms) is required due to the short time delay of an existing auto-reclose scheme. Systematic evaluation of the LoM relay performance both in terms of dependability and security is undertaken using Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) injection implemented on a Real-time Digital Simulator (RTDS). Based on the test results and detailed analysis, it is found that: 1) the objective of achieving fast RoCoF LoM detection (i.e. the dependability requirement) is feasible with the assumed settings but the protection security may be compromised under certain fault scenarios; 2) in addition to active power, the reactive power plays an important role in the RoCoF-based LoM detection; and 3) natural frequency oscillations following the fault clearance can lead to the unwanted RoCoF operation. These factors will need to be considered during the LoM setting process to ensure the proper balance between LOM protection dependability and security.

articleTitle: Enhancing wind turbine fault prediction through integrated SCADA data analysis and machine learning techniques
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Ensuring the resilience and protection of power systems is paramount in the integration of renewable energy sources such as wind turbines. This study introduces a sophisticated condition monitoring framework utilizing Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems alongside advanced machine learning techniques to enhance situational awareness and proactive maintenance. Focusing on critical events in wind turbine operations this research leverages a comprehensive dataset from the Penmanshiel wind farm, containing over 3.6 million SCADA records and detailed event logs spanning five years. Addressing challenges like high data dimensionality, complex non-linear relationships, and significant class imbalances, the methodology employs rigorous data preprocessing, including anomaly detection, data cleaning and data integration. Feature selection is optimized through Mutual Information and Lasso Regression, while Gradient Boosting algorithms, notably XGBoost and LightGBM, enhanced by Genetic Algorithms, provide robust predictive capabilities. The SMOTETomek technique ensures balanced datasets, resulting in models that achieve over 96% accuracy and F1-scores. Statistical validation via the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test confirms the significance of these improvements. This research contributes to power system resilience by enabling real-time situational awareness and protection-focused condition monitoring, facilitating proactive maintenance strategies that minimize downtime and enhance the reliability and stability of power infrastructures.

articleTitle: Interaction analysis between MMC-HVDC control and distance protection across multiple time scales
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Control systems for modular multilevel converter based high voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems involve numerous parameters and control loops, impacting AC system protection. This paper tries to answer the following question: Which control loops are more critical for impacting distance protection performance under different time scales? For this purpose, this study investigates the performance of key control loops, such as the phase-locked loop, fault current injection, total energy control, horizontal and vertical energy balancing, and current control across various time scales. By analyzing the impact of these loops during transient and steady-state periods, the study highlights their critical roles in optimizing distance protection during faults.

articleTitle: Principle of microgrid fault direction judgement based on transient wideband reactive power polarity
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Microgird fault characteristics varies depending on heterogeneous control scheme of distributed generation and shows growing relevance with it in off-grid operation, differentiated distributed power control strategies and grid operation modes therefore make it impossible to reliably judge fault directions, which leads to risk of misjudgment carried by conventional direction judgement method. In this paper, using the time window between fault and control act, a transient fault equivalent circuit for microgrid is established based on fault zero-state response, in which the response characteristics of each component in the system at different frequencies are analyzed and a transient equivalent model of each branch in a specific frequency band after the fault is constructed. This paper then put forward a principle of determining fault direction of microgrids using transient wideband reactive power polarity, which is not affected by the control characteristics of distributed power supply and the topology structure, also without the problem of voltage dead zone at near-end fault. With this principle accurate judgment of fault direction is realized under different fault types and fault location scenarios. The effectiveness of this direction element principle is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A double-layer protection scheme for PET based on fast directional pilot and high-frequency differential current
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper focuses on the three-port Power Electronic Transformer (PET) as the research object. Firstly, it briefly analyses the requirements for the relay protection configuration of the PET. Subsequently, the instantaneous electrical fault characteristics of each PET port under various fault types are studied. Then, the PET is deconstructed into two layers: an outer layer and an inner layer. For the outer layer, a rapid directional pilot protection based on the instantaneous power rate of change is proposed, which can target symmetric faults on the AC side and various types of faults on the DC side. For the inner layer, a high-frequency current differential protection is supplemented. Finally, the proposed double-layer protection is verified based on MATLAB/SIMULINK. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed protection scheme can reliably identify faults both inside and outside the protected zone, and possesses certain capabilities in transitioning resistance tolerance and noise immunity.

articleTitle: A high percentage distributed photovoltaic access boundary assessment method for different protection configuration scenarios
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic (PV) power generation technology, the proportion of distributed PV access to the grid is increasing, but this also brings new challenges to the security and stability of the grid. Currently, there are some problems in the protection configuration for PV access to the grid, such as the lack of a comprehensive assessment method for different access scenarios and the lack of a boundary calculation method for high percentage PV access. Therefore, this paper proposes a boundary assessment method for high-ratio distributed PV access with comprehensive consideration of different protection configuration scenarios, analyzes the distribution network under the influence of boosting effect, draw-out effect and reverse overcurrent, proposes an engineering calculation method for the boundary of the accessible capacity of distributed PV under different influences, and lists the access capacity and ratio boundary of the accessed distributed power supply under different scenarios. Finally, extensive simulations were conducted in the distribution network model using software. The simulation results verify the effectiveness and practicality of the distributed PV accessable capacity boundary calculation method.

articleTitle: Fault transient voltage support control for large-scale renewable power plant connecting to weak grid
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In the scenario of large-scale renewable power plant (RPP) connecting to weak grid, the opposite weak grid has difficulties to provide voltage support capacity during faults, leading to off-grid of RPP and causing safety problems of the whole system. Therefore, large-scale RPP should have fault transient voltage support capability. However, existing methods can only make RPP safe itself, not ensure safety of the power grid. Given this, a novel fault transient voltage support control strategy based on extended controllable boundary is proposed. The fault disturbance propagation is considered to build the extended controllable boundary, and the current command values are calculated through the grouping discrete mapping matrix. Referring to a typical scenario in Xinjiang, China, a simulation example is constructed in PSCAD, and the validation results show that the RPP can safely, exhaustively, fastly and flexibly provide transient voltage support capacity, with an improvement at least 40% when the voltage at PCC sags higher than 0.4p.u., compared to the current national standard.

articleTitle: Optimization of setting for ground distance protection in hybrid transmission lines with overhead lines and cables
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The hybrid lines consisting of overhead lines and cables alter the uniformity of transmission line impedance, leading to a contradiction between the reliability and sensitivity of ground distance protection. This paper analyzes the impact of the zero-sequence compensation coefficient of hybrid lines on ground distance protection. It investigates the monotonic variation characteristics of the zero-sequence compensation coefficient across different segments of hybrid transmission lines. An optimization method for comprehensively setting the zero-sequence compensation coefficient is proposed, considering connection points of hybrid lines, the end of the protection range, and the override of faults outside the protected zone. This enhances the reliability of ground distance protection in Section I for in-zone faults. Taking into account the sensitivity requirements of Section II and III of the ground distance protection, the paper presents methods for adaptive compensation of protection sensitivity coefficients and total impedance coefficients using comprehensive and maximum zero-sequence compensation coefficients, as well as comprehensive and total impedance zero-sequence compensation coefficients. These methods improve the sensitivity of ground distance protection actions for faults at the end of the line. The effectiveness of the setting optimization strategy proposed is verified through case studies. This setting optimization scheme has already been applied in actual power grids.

articleTitle: Differential equation algorithms for distance relays in the presence of inverter-based resources
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Distance protection is today one of the most common protection schemes and it traditionally applies phasor-based impedance estimation. However, as penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) grows, the phasor representation of voltages and currents is being challenged due to the fast control and nonlinear fault characteristics of IBRs, while the apparent impedance concept of Ohm’s law in distance relays relies on a linear time-invariant (LTI) system. In contrast, differential equation algorithms (DEAs) are model-based approaches trying to estimate the distance to the fault and not data-driven approaches. Hence, DEAs make no assumptions about the signal waveforms but rather the governing system itself. However, DEAs are not source independent, due to inaccuracies in the assumed system model, numerical errors and a limited sampling frequency to capture the system dynamics. This paper investigates these issues by analyzing the performance of DEAs in the presence of a grid-following inverter and a grid-forming inverter. Performance comparisons are made with the classical discrete Fourier transform (DFT) impedance estimation approach. Results indicate that the DEAs can with proper filtering yield distance estimates faster and with enhanced precision compared to the DFT for distance relay applications with IBRs. A sampling frequency of 5 kHz was sufficient and neglecting the stray capacitance of the transmission line model was adequate.

articleTitle: Fault recovery coordination control method adapted to line reclosing for distribution networks with photovoltaic-storage-charging station
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In the active distribution network including photovoltaic, energy storage and charging stations, the anti-island protection after fault of the transmission line will cut out the renewable energy sources (RESs), and the RESs will be connected to the grid after the successful line coincidence. This practice will result in RES outages and distribution network power supply interruption, failing to fully utilize the temporary island operation capabilities of new sources and loads. Therefore, a coordinated control method for fault recovery of distribution network with photovoltaic-storage-charging station adapted to line reclosing is proposed. First, the isolated island operation scheme of photovoltaic-storage-charging station during line reclosing is developed, and the power sources and loads matching method is proposed. The power balance scheme is determined according to the mode of load importance and load-weighted maximum power conservation. Second, during the islanding operation, the control mode of the inverter-type DG in the photovoltaic-storage-charging station is switched to virtual synchronous machine (VSG) control to give it the capability of short-term islanding operation. Third, after the fault is cleared, the circuit breaker near the main network side recloses by checking no voltage, the circuit breaker near the distribution network side recloses by checking synchronous, and reliable synchronization with the voltage of the main network side is realized through the active control of the photovoltaic-storage-charging station, reducing the impact of the impulse current on the new energy power source. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed fault recovery coordination strategy is verified by MATLAB/Simulink simulation examples.

articleTitle: Hardware in loop simulation of replay attacks on synchrophasor data and detection using machine learning approach
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: In the 21stcentury, the power system has integrated large-scale communication technology with existing infrastructure, enabling wide-area monitoring, protection, and control (WAMPAC) applications. Though this has enhanced the grid’s reliability, stability, security, and operations, it has also increased its dependency on communication networks, resulting in new cybersecurity issues. Among various cyber-attacks, Replay attacks have received less attention due to their similarity to healthy scenarios, making them difficult to detect. This article presents a machine learning (ML) approach using Random Forest (RF) to detect Replay attacks in Synchrophasor data. The method classifies data as either "Healthy" or "Replay-attack" by extracting statistical features such as mean, standard deviation, variance, skewness, kurtosis and auto-correlation. The algorithm’s effectiveness is evaluated by comparing different metrics with models like Support Vector Machines (SVM) andk-Nearest Neighbour(k-NN). To validate the proposed method, a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) cyber-physical testbed was developed, and various datasets for training and validation were generated. Synchrophasor data, from a Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) to a Phasor Data Concentrator (PDC), are generated using network emulation software containing both healthy cases and attack scenarios. The comparative analysis of the results demonstrates that the proposed model outperforms SVM andk-NN, thereby accurately detecting Replay attacks.

articleTitle: Sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) protection algorithm utilizing advanced signal processing techniques
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative approach to protect power systems against sub-synchronous resonance (SSR) utilizing advanced signal processing techniques. The methodology integrates an Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) preprocessing filter to effectively isolate the dominant sub-synchronous component, an Adaptive Notch Filter (ANF) for real-time frequency tracking and amplitude estimation while suppressing noise, and a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter to extract the fundamental component's rate of change for robust blocking logic. Validation against the IEEE SSR First Benchmark Model in MATLAB/Simulink demonstrates its efficacy in ensuring power system stability and reliability under SSR conditions. Furthermore, field validation utilizing SSR recording data from a Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind farm located in Finland demonstrates its robustness across various operational environments.

articleTitle: Fault location for mixed two and three terminal overhead and underground cable transmission circuits
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Locating a fault precisely on power transmission lines is highly advantageous to power utilities in expediting the repair of the faulted components, speeding up the restoration of power supply, thereby reducing outage time and the financial burden on utilities. Several fault location methods including impedance and traveling wave based are commercially available for conventional transmission lines. However, fault location in mixed circuits (combined overhead and underground/subsea cables) is difficult due to different impedance parameters for each section and lack of junction measurements. In this paper, innovative faulted section identification and fault location solution is developed using all side voltage and current measurements for two and three terminal mixed lines. Faulted section identification is very important input for the fault location solution. For two terminal mixed lines, faulted section is identified by checking the sign of the calculated faulted section identification indices. The faulted section identification indices are calculated using the ratio of difference of voltage and current at each junction of the mixed line. The junction voltage and current are calculated from both terminals using each section parameters and positive sequence voltage and current measurements. For three terminal mixed lines, faulted section is identified by comparing the differences of calculated and measured voltage at each terminal. The faulted location is calculated using the faulted section identification information, each section parameters and during fault phasors. The proposed solution is verified using laboratory experimental and field data and it is found to be accurate. The solution is implemented in the existing line differential relay platform using 1kHz sampling rate and it does not need any additional infrastructural changes.

articleTitle: Functional splitting in multivendor HVDC grid protection
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Moving towards truly multivendor HVDC grids requires definition of the functional performance at the system and device level, as well as decision making on control and protection architecture. While many technical solutions to solve protection system challenges have been developed and demonstrated in the past decade – e.g. DC circuit breakers and protection relays – there is still no consensus on how to divide the required functionality across different physical devices. This is particularly of interest for multivendor systems, in which well defined functional requirements must be developed for the individual devices and their interfaces. This paper examines a method to perform the splitting of protection system functionality, enabling systematic rules to be applied when choosing a protection system implementation in a multivendor system where different parties have different interests. Behavioural or functional modelling of the system, e.g. using Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), is applied to describe the system and enable choices in splitting of functionality between different physical devices and/or devices from different manufacturers.

articleTitle: Adoption and implementation of IEC 61850 process bus technology in Davao Light and Power Company: learnings and strategies
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: IEC61850 has now been accepted ‘almost unequivocally’ as the preferred standard for substation communications. Utilities and industries across the world are at various stages of adoption of this standard. The extent of utilization of this standard in the majority of installations around the world is at “station bus” level with IEC 61850-8-1 reporting and GOOSE. Moving further along the digitization chain, it is foreseen that numerous benefits can be availed if process values (e.g. currents/voltages/switchgear status) are digitized as close to the source as possible (i.e. in the switchyard) and utilized in automation system. Davao Light and Power Company (Davao Light) is the third largest privately-owned electric distribution utility in the Philippines in terms of customer size and annual kWh sales. Davao Light is witnessing significant electricity demand growth and penetration of renewable generation sources. These requirements motivated Davao Light to look out for ways to achieve efficiency in delivering substation projects. Digital substations with process bus technology help to reduce CAPEX and OPEX significantly and achieve sustainable and efficient design while maintaining a reliable network. Adoption of new technology in an environment such as substations, where reliability is of paramount importance, needs to be carefully planned. Davao Light considered various aspects such as engineering, organizational impact, long term stability, whole-of-life benefits, standardization and re-usable engineering before embarking on this journey. We have a few digital substations already in operation and the return-on-experience validates our assumptions. This paper describes the process that preceded the selection of digital substation technology, design principles that were followed and our experience during execution and operation that fed into improvements. We envisage that digital substation technology not only provides immediate savings but prepares an infrastructure on which future technologies can be integrated.

articleTitle: Next-generation disturbance prevention and supply restoration for holistic supply reliability and safety
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: Supplying 80% of Hong Kong’s population with electricity, CLP Power Hong Kong Limited (CLP Power) strives for excellence in reliability and safety despite challenges such as increasing adverse weather events. While protection systems are the foundation for the safe operation in the case of system disturbance, CLP Power implements a holistic approach to minimise the emergence of a disturbance and, if it does occur, to accelerate supply restoration time. This paper therefore introduces four initiatives as examples for this holistic approach. In the pre-disturbance phase, the Asset Health Management System (AHMS) and AI-supported drone-based condition monitoring allow condition-based maintenance to prevent potential disturbances. Post-disturbance, to quickly return to normal operation and restore supply, CLP Power has deployed an automatic restoration system and solutions using the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI). These solutions increase supply reliability and safety, enhance operational efficiency and resources allocation.

articleTitle: Application of a digital substation technology to offshore wind farms challenges and opportunities
publicationTitle: 18th International Conference on Developments in Power System Protection (DPSP APAC 2025)
abstract: The offshore wind industry is growing rapidly as many countries have committed to using this affordable renewable energy source to lower greenhouse gas emissions, tackle global climate change, and ultimately achieve net zero carbon targets. Massive deployment of large-scale offshore wind farms (OWF) around the globe requires application of innovative solutions to optimize design, accelerate project execution schedules, and safely achieve first power dates as well as improve availability, reliability, and monitoring capabilities for the assets in operation and increase key indicators for Quality Heath Safety and Environment (QHSE). Application of a Digital Substation (DSS) technology to OWFs opens prospects for harvesting the above-mentioned benefits given that all the specific aspects of such projects are properly considered. The shift from conventional towards digital substation design implies digitalization of analog and binary hardwire interfaces between the primary system (high-voltage (HV) equipment) and secondary system (protection, control, metering, SCADA, and other low-voltage (LV) systems) as well as interfaces within secondary systems based on IEC 61850 collection of standards. The paper discusses in detail the expected benefits, challenges, and risks associated with the application of DSS technology to OWFs. All these aspects are analysed considering the specifics of such projects and followed by the proposals for enabling the successful implementation of the technology.
